summary: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is a postgraduate scholarship at the University of Cambridge for citizens of any country outside the United Kingdom. It is run by the Gates Cambridge Trust and supports full-time PhD, MLitt, and most full-time one-year postgraduate courses (a part-time PhD option is a pilot). It pays the University composition fee, a maintenance allowance, airfares and visa costs, with optional extra grants. Scholars are chosen for academic excellence, the reasons for their course, commitment to improving others' lives and leadership. One combined application covers admission and funding.
eligibility_notes:
Citizenship: the applicant must be a citizen of a country outside the United Kingdom. Dual citizens of the UK and another country are eligible (FAQ).

Courses: the applicant must be applying to a full-time PhD (part-time PhD funding is a pilot), a full-time MLitt, or a full-time one-year postgraduate course at Cambridge, with some exceptions. Master's courses named as eligible in the FAQ are MPhil, MLitt, MRes and LLM, and master's study must be full-time. Not considered: any undergraduate degree (including a second BA), MASt courses, part-time degrees other than the PhD, and professional or non-standard degrees. The excluded list names the MBA, Executive MBA and Global Executive MBA, Master of Finance, Executive Master of Accounting, Business Doctorate, PGCE, MBBChir Clinical Studies, the six-year part-time MD (home students only), the Graduate Course in Medicine (A101) and the Master of Conservation of Easel Painting. The FAQ also names PGCert, PGDip and MSt as not eligible, and the Doctor of Education.

Current Cambridge students: they may apply for a new postgraduate course (for example a PhD after an MPhil), and current Gates Cambridge scholars may apply for a second scholarship for a new degree. All current Cambridge students are considered in the second round. A student cannot apply to fund the rest of a course already started.

Academic level and grades: no minimum GPA is set. Academic excellence is judged as a whole (transcripts, references, experience and potential); Cambridge departments put forward only the most academically outstanding applicants. A second master's does not make an applicant ineligible, but the applicant should explain why.

Language: the scholarship has no English test of its own; the University of Cambridge has its own requirement.

Other funding: the scholarship can be held with another award, but duplicate money such as two maintenance payments is not allowed. The Trust discusses shared arrangements. Admissions are needs-blind.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work-experience requirement are stated.
funding_summary: The scholarship pays the University composition fee at the applicable rate, a maintenance allowance (GBP 23,152 for 12 months for a single student at the 2026-27 rate, paid pro rata for shorter courses and for PhD scholars up to 4 years), one economy single airfare at the start and one at the end of the course, and inbound visa costs plus the Immigration Health Surcharge. Discretionary grants cover academic development, children, fieldwork, parental intermission and hardship. If another scholarship or salary is received, the maintenance allowance may be reduced or withheld.
programmes_note: Eligible courses are the PhD, the full-time MLitt and full-time one-year postgraduate courses such as MPhil, MRes and LLM. Any subject Cambridge teaches at these levels is allowed; the scholarship sets no subject limit. PhD and most research MPhil applicants must contact a possible supervisor and include a summary of a research project developed with them; taught MPhil and other applicants explain how the course advances their career plans. Exclusions are listed in the eligibility notes.
institutions_note: The scholarship funds study at the University of Cambridge only. Admission and funding are one application made through the University's Graduate Application Portal; the Trust can see the whole application. Admission offers are decided separately from funding, so an applicant may receive an admission offer before the funding result.

summary.detail: Full-time one-year master's courses at Cambridge: MPhil, MLitt, MRes and LLM (master's study must be full-time). Not eligible: PGCert, PGDip, MSt, MASt, MBA, EMBA, MFin, PGCE and the Graduate Course in Medicine. Master's applicants state how the course advances their plans; research MPhil applicants also give a research project summary developed with a supervisor.

benefits.limit_text: University composition fee at the appropriate rate
benefits.conditions: If the applicant wins a fee award from a public body such as UKRI, they should accept it, and the Trust may then not pay the fee or may share fee and maintenance costs.

benefits.limit_text: GBP 23,152 for 12 months for a single student (2026-27 rate)
benefits.conditions: Shorter courses are paid pro rata. PhD scholars receive it for up to 4 years. The Trust may reduce or withhold it if the scholar has a salary or another substantial scholarship.

benefits.limit_text: One economy single airfare at the start and one at the end of the course
Inbound visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge
Academic development grant GBP 750 to GBP 4,000, depending on course length
benefits.conditions: Discretionary, case by case, for conferences and courses.

benefits.limit_text: Dependent Children Allowance up to GBP 12,793 a year for one child, or up to GBP 18,244 a year for two or more
benefits.conditions: Discretionary. No funding is given for a partner.

benefits.limit_text: Fieldwork, parental intermission (up to 6 months with maintenance) and hardship support
benefits.conditions: Discretionary. During PhD fieldwork a scholar can apply to keep the normal maintenance allowance; other fieldwork costs are expected to come from the composition fee.

benefits.limit_text: Bench fees, scientific equipment and the University application fee
benefits.conditions: The department is expected to cover core course costs. The University offers application-fee waivers.

requirements.text: Four written answers to the Gates Cambridge questions inside the funding section of the application, using specific examples: academic excellence (about 200 words, up to 1,400 characters); why this Cambridge course and how it fits future plans (about 200 words, 1,400 characters); commitment to improving others' lives and its link to the future (about 300 words, 2,100 characters); leadership capacity and how it will help make an impact (about 300 words, 2,100 characters).
The admission section of the Cambridge application: chosen course, college preference, academic background, plans and suitability.

A research proposal. Most applicants upload it with the admission documents; applicants for other degrees do not need one. PhD and most research MPhil applicants must also contact a possible supervisor and include a summary of a research project developed with them.
requirements.conditional_rule: PhD applicants (and most research MPhil applicants for the supervisor contact)

requirements.text: Two academic references for admission, plus a separate Gates Cambridge reference on intellectual ability, course choice, commitment to others and leadership. The Gates referee rates the applicant as exceptional, strong, not strong or weak and states the group and its size. The reference is up to 4,000 characters typed or an uploaded letter. It can be written by one of the academic referees if they address the criteria rather than repeat the academic reference; friends and family are not suitable.
Academic records required by the Cambridge admission application (transcripts of previous study). The Gates Cambridge pages do not list the individual documents.

application_steps.title: Make one combined application in the Cambridge portal
application_steps.detail: Admission and funding are one application in the University's Graduate Application Portal, and the Trust can see all of it. Complete the admission section (course, college preference, academic background, plans, suitability) and the Gates Cambridge part of the funding section; both are needed for consideration. Each course application needs its own funding section, and submitted applications cannot be edited.

application_steps.title: Write the selection answers and add the research proposal
application_steps.detail: Answer the four selection questions with specific examples within the word limits. PhD applicants include a research proposal, which most upload with their admission documents. Check the round: Round 1 is for US citizens living in the USA, and Round 2 (the larger round) is for everyone else, including US citizens living, studying or working abroad and all current Cambridge students. Round 2 deadlines depend on the course.

application_steps.title: Line up your references before the deadline
application_steps.detail: Arrange two academic references for admission and a Gates Cambridge reference. Brief referees on the criteria and ask for concrete examples. All references must be in by the deadline. The 2025/6 cycle allowed up to 7 applications; the limit for 2027/8 was not stated.

application_steps.title: Cambridge departments rank and nominate applicants
application_steps.detail: Cambridge academic departments nominate a small number of eligible applicants who meet all four criteria to a very high level: academic excellence, reasons for the choice of course, commitment to improving the lives of others, and leadership capacity. Applicants not nominated receive an email saying they were unsuccessful. Round 1 applicants hear about this stage in early December; others by early March.

application_steps.title: Interview and subject panel review
application_steps.detail: Nominated candidates are invited to a 25 to 30 minute interview, in person or online, with one of four subject panels (Arts, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences, Social Sciences). The panel talks about knowledge of the scholarship and motivation, academic and career plans, and gives time for questions. Candidates nominated for several courses choose one to interview for. Panels sit in January 2027 (Round 1) and in March 2027 (Round 2).

application_steps.title: Scholarships are offered
application_steps.detail: Offers go out by early February 2027 (Round 1) and by early April 2027 (Round 2). No feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants, including after interview, and an unsuccessful application does not harm later applications. Interview accommodation (one night) and parking are covered when needed.

application_steps.title: Accept the offer quickly
application_steps.detail: A scholarship offer must be accepted within 72 hours. Admission to Cambridge is decided separately, so the scholar must also hold the admission offer for the funded course.

application_steps.title: Report other funding and use the extra grants
application_steps.detail: Scholars must tell the Trust as soon as possible about any funding toward the Cambridge degree, because salary or another substantial scholarship can reduce the maintenance allowance. Scholars can apply for the discretionary grants for academic development, children, fieldwork, parental intermission and hardship.
